title: The Python SDK's two ZCC clients: OneAPI service and legacy helper
aliases: zcc python 3 calls per day error

prose.text: The Python SDK reaches ZCC through either the OneAPI client or a legacy helper that signs in with ZCC portal keys. How each path authenticates is in [[zcc.api.authentication]]; this subject holds what the Python clients themselves do.

prose.label: Legacy sign-in.
prose.text: {{legacy-token-refresh}} {{legacy-exit-no-logout}} The login call and token header are [[zcc.api.authentication:legacy-login-request]] and [[zcc.api.authentication:legacy-auth-token-header]]; the host the helper builds is in [[zcc.api.authentication:legacy-host]]. The partner header is [[zia.sdk-python.authentication:partner-id-header]].

prose.label: Legacy limits and retries.
prose.text: The helper's counters and 429 handling are [[zcc.api.rate-limits:legacy-local-counters]], [[zcc.api.rate-limits:legacy-429-retry]] and [[zcc.api.rate-limits:legacy-download-raise]]. {{legacy-preflight-message}} {{legacy-network-retries}}

prose.label: OneAPI retries.
prose.text: The OneAPI executor's wait comes from [[zcc.api.rate-limits:oneapi-retry-headers]]. Whether an OneAPI-fronted ZCC 429 carries those headers at all is open {{gap:oneapi-429-headers}}.

two-client-paths.statement: On a OneAPI client, `client.zcc` is a `ZCCService` built on first use and kept. On a client constructed for legacy use, `client.zcc` returns the legacy ZCC helper object itself, and raises RuntimeError when no legacy helper was supplied.

legacy-client-env.statement: `LegacyZCCClient` takes `api_key`, `secret_key` and `cloud` from its config dictionary, falling back to the environment variables `ZCC_CLIENT_ID`, `ZCC_CLIENT_SECRET` and `ZCC_CLOUD`; the helper defaults the cloud to `zscaler` when none is given.

legacy-missing-secrets.statement: The legacy helper exposes the same ZCC service properties as `ZCCService` except `secrets`, so `get_otp` and `get_passwords` are not reachable through `client.zcc` on a legacy client.
legacy-missing-secrets.conditions: Absence: legacy.py defines properties for devices, admin_user, company, entitlements, forwarding_profile, fail_open_policy, web_policy, web_app_service, web_privacy, trusted_networks, application_profiles and the three app catalogs, and no `secrets` property.

legacy-token-refresh.statement: The legacy helper calls its token refresh before every request; it logs in again when it holds no token or the token has expired, and raises a plain Exception, 'Failed to login using provided credentials.', when the login fails.

legacy-exit-no-logout.statement: Exiting the legacy ZCC helper as a context manager (its `__exit__`) only writes a debug log line; unlike the ZIA legacy client it sends no logout request.

legacy-preflight-message.statement: When a local counter is exhausted, the helper raises AttributeError ('str' object has no attribute 'isoformat') instead of its ValueError messages, because the exception class it raises requires a datetime.

legacy-network-retries.statement: On a transport error (`requests.RequestException`) the legacy helper sleeps five seconds and sends the same request again, up to three attempts in all, without regard to the HTTP method, so a POST or PUT whose response was lost is sent again.

oneapi-429-headers.title: Which rate-limit headers a ZCC 429 carries on the OneAPI path
oneapi-429-headers.blocks: telling how long the Python OneAPI executor waits after a ZCC 429, or whether it gives up without retrying
oneapi-429-headers.detail: Unverified legacy statement: an OneAPI-fronted ZCC 429 may emit `X-Rate-Limit-Remaining` or `X-Rate-Limit-Retry-After-Seconds`, exposed unchanged to the shared executor. The executor reads `Retry-After`, then the reset headers, then `X-Rate-Limit-Retry-After-Seconds`, then `X-Rate-Limit-Remaining` as seconds, and returns an error when none is present. Drive a OneAPI ZCC call to 429 and record the response headers.
